full_judgment:
6. The High Court Division held that the settlement of the suit land with the plaintiffs was not approved of by the Chief Manager of the Nawab Estate and therefore Ext. 2 and 2(a) would not confer any title upon the plaintiffs. It also held that the plaintiffs having not taken any steps to lodge any claim under the then Private Forest Act. 1949, the discretionary relief under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act cannot be granted to the plaintiffs. 

 7. In disposing of the petition for leave to appeal, this Division held that the plaintiffs case was dismissed by the trial Court and the High Court Division because they failed to prove their own case of settlement. The trial Court found the documents of the plaintiffs as fabricated. The lower appellate Court did not reverse the finding of the trial Court as to the fraudulent nature of the documents but additionally found that the settlement was not granted by the competent authority to grant settlement, namely, the Chief Manager of the Dhaka Nawab Court of Ward Estate. In the face of these findings, it was held, "it does not lie in the mouth of the plaintiffs to challenge the constitution of reserve Forest. They have not proved their own case of settlement." 

 9. The court of appeal below reversed the finding of the trial Court and found that the settlement was validly taken by the plaintiffs and the trial Court missed the point that the term 'Manager' also includes 'Assistant Manager' and there was no illegality about the sanction order passed by the Assistant Manager. Consequently, the lower appellate Court by giving certain reasons believed the settlement of the plaintiffs. The lower appellate Court, of course, did not reverse the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiffs in collusion with the tahsilder and other employees of Begunbari Tahsil Office fabricated their documents namely, salami receipt, Ext. 2 and 2 (a), rent receipts, Ext. 3 series and Ext. 4. 5(a) and Ext. 6 series The lower appellate Court as a final court of fact was, of course competent to construe the document in its own way by holding the same as a valid document of title. 

 10. The material question in revision before the learned judge of the High Court Division was, whether the vital documents of settlement of the plaintiffs were properly construed by the court of appeal below. A construction of document is of course, a mixed question of law and fact and the same having not been properly construed by the lower appellate Court the High Court Division was within its competence to reverse that finding after giving cogent reason. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division found that the document creating lease in favor of the plaintiffs having been executed by a person having no lawful authority the same would not confer any title to the plaintiff. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division found that the salami receipts were not granted by the Chief Manager of the Dhaka Nawab Estate who was competent to approve the settlement and consequently the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division after reversing the finding of the lower appellate Court held that by dint of Ext. 2 and 2(a), salami receipts no lease was granted in favor of the plaintiffs. Thus it cannot be said as has been argued by Mr. SR Pal, learned Advocate for the appellants, that the lower appellate Court having reversed the finding of the trial Court on giving valid reasons the same cannot be interfered with by the High Court Division and this Division ignored its own established practice in this regard by accepting the finding of the High Court Division.
